claim: run_memory_call submits the call to a one-worker ThreadPoolExecutor and awaits it through asyncio.wrap_future; cancelling the awaiting task cancels the concurrent Future when it has not started (so the call never runs), and leaves a started call running to completion.
verify_against: CPython asyncio.futures.wrap_future / _chain_future cancellation propagation and concurrent.futures.Future.cancel semantics for running futures
verify_hint: Check asyncio.futures._chain_future (_call_check_cancel calls source.cancel()) and concurrent.futures.Future.cancel, which returns False once the future is RUNNING; compare with run_memory_call in src/sqllens/memory/store.py

claim: On caller cancellation, run_memory_call attaches _log_call_after_cancel as a done callback; it logs nothing if the concurrent Future was cancelled, logs INFO naming the function on success, and WARNING with exc_info on failure, including when the future had already completed before the callback was attached.
verify_against: concurrent.futures.Future.add_done_callback (invokes immediately when already done) and Future.exception() behavior
verify_hint: Check _log_call_after_cancel and the except asyncio.CancelledError branch of run_memory_call in src/sqllens/memory/store.py against concurrent.futures.Future.add_done_callback

claim: The docstring asserts that calls run one at a time in submission order, that a caller cancelled before its call starts drops it, that a started call runs to completion with later calls waiting behind it and its outcome logged, and that exceptions propagate unchanged.
source_excerpt:
Calls run one at a time in submission order. A caller cancelled before its
    call starts drops it; a call already started runs to completion, later
    calls wait behind it, and its outcome is logged (``INFO`` on success,
    ``WARNING`` with the exception on failure). Exceptions propagate unchanged.
verify_against: _get_executor (max_workers=1) and run_memory_call in src/sqllens/memory/store.py; ThreadPoolExecutor work-queue FIFO behavior
verify_hint: Trace two run_memory_call submissions from different event loops (the server loop and a CLI asyncio.run loop in one process) and a caller cancelled in the window after the worker dequeues the item but before it is marked running; check whether ordering and the 'drops it' outcome still hold

claim: The doc's cancellation bullet asserts a call cancelled while queued never runs; a started call runs to completion with later calls waiting behind it even though admin_write_lock/import_lock are released when the cancelled task unwinds; and run_memory_call logs the outcome at INFO naming the store function on success or WARNING with exception and traceback on failure.
source_excerpt: A call cancelled while it waits in the queue never runs. A call that has started runs to completion, and calls submitted after it wait behind it, even though the `asyncio.Lock`s the handlers hold (`admin_write_lock`, `import_lock`) are released as soon as the cancelled task unwinds.
